name: Civil unrest
value: France protests shrink; Istanbul media march
summary: French living-cost protests shrink after concessions; thousands march in Istanbul on 22 Nov against a media crackdown
state: France's living-cost protests drew 82,500 people nationwide on 21 Nov, the lowest of six Saturdays, after government wage and school-aid concessions (Bloomberg). Several thousand people marched in Istanbul on 22 Nov against a crackdown on opposition media that saw a trustee appointed to Sözcü TV; no violence was reported (Turkish Minute). Significant protests in several countries keep Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest or major crackdown in a large country was found as of 25 Nov.
for_you: Protests can disrupt transport and city centres at short notice. Travellers can check FCDO travel advice for the countries concerned.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests in several countries (France, Turkey); no deadly nationwide unrest

sources.title: Bloomberg — France's cost of living protests shrink as government offers wage, school aid
Turkish Minute — Thousands rally in İstanbul against crackdown on Turkish media

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
